description:
Requested by the user, verbatim (relayed by Optimize 2026-11-20): "file the TRMC gap as a ticket that Callables agent should handle at it's next opportunity." Owner: Callables, at its next opportunity.

Evidence (Optimize's probe, 2026-11-20, release fz2 built 2026-11-18, fz2 run, 1,000,000 elements): no stack overflow, but continuation_allocs 2,000,261 and continuation_bytes 96,016,400, one 48-byte heap continuation per element per function. Tail recursion modulo cons would allocate none. Owned-cons reuse works: list_cons_allocs is 2,000,001, not 3M, because app relinks inc's private cells.

```elixir
defmodule T do
  def inc([]), do: []
  def inc([h | t]), do: [h + 1 | inc(t)]
  def app([], ys), do: ys
  def app([h | t], ys), do: [h | app(t, ys)]
end

def main() do
  xs = Enum.to_list(1..1_000_000)
  ys = T.inc(xs)
  zs = T.app(ys, [0])
  dbg(length(zs))
  dbg(Process.heap_alloc_stats())
end
```

The docs already claim the mechanism: guides/memory.html:347-355 ("builds the list forward with an O(1) continuation (tail recursion modulo cons)") and README.md:362-366 (a callee whose list's eventual tail is known builds its cells pointing at that tail). The guide is also stale: ReturnDemand no longer exists (now ShapeDemand / ExecutableNeed), and fixtures/quicksort is now fixtures/01577_quicksort.

First step: re-run the probe on a current develop binary, since fz-9x7's heap-continuation work may have moved it.

Done when:
- the probe shape on interp, run and build reports continuation_allocs independent of list length, with cells written front to back into the destination hole;
- an oracle fixture pins that with heap_alloc_stats;
- a bench A/B is done;
- guides/memory.html, README and .agent/docs state the mechanism as built, with current names.
title: A body-recursive list builder fills its tail in place, with no continuation per element
